jobs.description:
Summary

At Apple, we work every single day to craft products that enrich people’s lives. Do you love working on challenges that no one has solved yet? Do you like changing the game? As a member of our PMU team at our Nabern office close to Stuttgart, you will have the great opportunity to craft upcoming products that will delight and encourage millions of Apple’s customers every day! We are looking for an AMS Verification Engineer who will enable us to verify our next generation of PMUs, in close collaboration with the design teams. The responsibilities include contributing to the top level verification of our PMUs. A number of IP specific features as well as interaction between IPs will also be part of the expected verification scope.

Description

- In this role, you will take care of ensuring high quality silicon for IC chips and IPs. The workflow starts with careful review of specifications followed by crafting of a verification plan and schedule. Then the verification is executed according to plan to support tape-out. - Execution of verification plans from beginning to end: test bench and environment bring-up, regressions, failure debug, and tape-out - Develop detailed test and coverage plans based on IC specifications - Develop verification methodology suitable for the IP, ensuring scalability and portability - Develop verification environment, including stimuli, checkers, assertions, trackers, and coverage - Sign-off mixed signal designs in preparation for tape-out.

Minimum Qualifications

- Bachelors in EE or related field, or equivalent work experience
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, combined with the ability to collaborate
- Ability to work well on a team, take ownership and motivate self and others
- Fluent English skills

Preferred Qualifications

- Advanced knowledge of mixed signal verification
- Few years of experience in industry for production integrated circuits.
- Experience with developments in hardware descriptive languages: Verilog, System-Verilog, and/or Verilog-AMS code.
- A background that includes scripting or programming languages is preferred. These include, but are not limited to, TCL, Skill, Python, and/or PERL.
- Familiar with analog behavioural models
- Familiar with verification methodologies and tools: simulators, waveform viewers, execution automation, coverage collection, experience developing scalable and portable test cases
- Possess sufficient analog IC background to identify failure possibilities, work through first order debug, and analyse analog verification results
- Knowledge of analog concurrent assertion and static analyses checks is a plus
- Understanding of both power management and related auxiliary circuitry: switching converters, linear converters, reference circuitry, band-gaps, data converters, and clock generators

jobs.description:
Summary

Would you like to be part of Apple’s fast-growing RF wireless design team in Munich? We are responsible for all aspects of wireless silicon development with a particular emphasis on highly integrated, power efficient designs and advanced semiconductor technologies that enable an outstanding user experience. IC design engineers work on circuit and system solutions for sophisticated wireless chips. This is a highly visible role in a fast growing silicon design group where you'll have the opportunity to make a critical impact on getting innovative consumer products to a global customer base quickly!

Description

As a RF Design Engineer at Apple, you will use your vast background in circuit design and provide PLL design solutions for wireless chips. You will collaborate with platform architects, system group, and digital design group to define the requirements for a PLL lineup based on the product requirements. You will also work with the Apple technology team and silicon foundries on process evaluation/selection for the target device. Design tasks include various analog biasing blocks, oscillators, frequency dividers and local oscillator chains. You will work with system engineering, layout, and chip integration teams to integrate the IP’s and verify the top-level functionality and performance. You also will work with RF test engineers to bring up, characterize and optimize new silicon.

Minimum Qualifications

- Profound experience in RF circuit design techniques.
- Experience with Cadence design tools.
- EM modelling and simulation skills.
- MSEE /PhD or equivalent is required.
- Proficiency in English is required.

Preferred Qualifications

- A proven track record in RF, and analog integrated circuit design, with experience in wireless PLL circuit architectures in CMOS technologies.
- Deep understanding in PLL system specifications and the ability to work with system architects to translate system requirements into circuit requirements at IC block level. 
- Knowledge in fundamental RF theories and concepts, such as innovative PLL concepts and their trade-offs in key performance parameters (KPI’s), area and power efficiency.
- The ability to optimize the overall PLL system including EVM, blocker requirements and crosstalk mitigations.
- Deep technical knowledge in analysis, design, and implementation of RF wireless low-noise, broadband and power efficient PLLs, as well as frequency converting blocks.
- Extensive experience in simulation of RF analog key building blocks, such as oscillators, frequency dividers, phase detectors and local oscillator signal distribution chains
- Solid experience in optimization of RF circuit design impairments by means of highly sophisticated methods of trimming and calibration 
- Experience in RF cross talk analysis, understanding the critical RF cross talk building laws and the according aggressor and victim analysis, translation of RF system KPI's into IC block level isolation requirements 
- Understanding of RF device modelling, insights into packaging effects, integrated coils, supply isolations, high frequency ESD structures, and circuit layout for optimum performance.
- Hands-on experience in high frequency silicon characterization and debugging on chip as well as on system level.

Senior Electrical Systems Engineer (m/f/d)

Instrumentation, Controls & Power Systems

Help Accelerate Industrial Decarbonization

Join exceptional people from around the world to solve some of the world's toughest energy challenges, make a real impact, and enjoy the adventure of building the future of industrial decarbonization together.

As our Senior Electrical Systems Engineer (m/f/d) – Instrumentation, Controls & Power Systems, you will play a key role in designing the electrical infrastructure that powers GlassPoint's next generation of solar thermal plants.

Working closely with colleagues across Mechanical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Systems Engineering, EPC partners, and suppliers, you will develop safe, reliable, and efficient electrical solutions for industrial-scale renewable energy facilities.

From concept development through commissioning, you'll contribute to projects that are shaping the future of industrial heat and energy.

Your Impact

In this role, you'll design electrical systems that enable the safe and efficient operation of some of the world's largest solar thermal facilities, supporting heavy industry on its journey toward decarbonization.

You'll combine technical expertise with systems thinking, working with internal teams, EPC partners, and global suppliers to develop robust, scalable electrical solutions that become part of our commercial projects worldwide.

What You'll Do

Design Electrical Systems

- Develop the conceptual design of electrical systems for solar thermal plants.
- Design and specify electrical heat tracing (EHT) systems, including piping, tanks, cable routing, junction boxes, and interfaces to plant control systems.
- Develop electrical architectures that support reliable, efficient, and safe plant operation.
- Ensure compliance with applicable international standards, regulations, and engineering best practices.

Develop Instrumentation & Control Systems

- Specify instrumentation including temperature, pressure, flow, and level measurement devices.
- Collaborate with Controls Engineering teams to define automation concepts, control philosophies, and system interfaces.
- Develop instrumentation and control (I&C) architectures for molten-salt solar thermal systems.
- Support the development of tracking algorithms, automation solutions, and electrical control strategies.

Engineering & Supplier Collaboration

- Select and specify electrical drive systems for solar collector tracking.
- Prepare technical specifications and tender documentation.
- Evaluate supplier solutions and support technical decision-making.
- Collaborate with engineering partners, control system providers, and equipment vendors throughout the project lifecycle.
- Manage technical interfaces and support successful project execution.

Support Project Delivery

- Support prototype development, testing, commissioning, and troubleshooting.
- Work collaboratively across disciplines to resolve technical challenges.
- Contribute to the development and improvement of electrical design standards and engineering processes.
- Provide technical expertise throughout all project phases, from concept development through commissioning.

Who You Are

You enjoy solving complex engineering challenges and designing reliable systems for demanding industrial environments. You combine strong technical expertise with a practical, solution-oriented mindset and have experience managing external partners and vendors. You thrive in multidisciplinary teams, communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and balance attention to detail with system-level thinking. Curious, collaborative, and eager to learn, you enjoy helping build engineering processes in a growing technology company while working both independently and as part of a team.

Ideally, you'll bring

- Master's degree (or equivalent) in Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field.
- Several years of experience designing electrical systems for industrial plants, renewable energy projects, power generation facilities, or process industries.
- Strong experience in electrical engineering, instrumentation, and control system design.
- Experience designing or specifying electrical heat tracing (EHT) systems and associated electrical infrastructure.
- Solid understanding of electrical power distribution and component selection.
- Experience with electrical drives, motors, and motion systems.
- Knowledge of industrial instrumentation, including temperature, pressure, flow, and level measurement technologies.
- Experience with process wiring, cable design, and electrical documentation.
- Understanding of low-voltage protection concepts and electrical safety principles.
- Experience creating technical documentation such as P&IDs, loop diagrams, and equipment specifications.
- Familiarity with international engineering standards such as IEC and VDE; knowledge of NEC is beneficial.
- Experience with PLC programming, industrial automation, or control software would be an advantage.
- Interest in microprocessor-based systems and edge controllers.
- Experience working with suppliers, contractors, or external engineering partners.
- Strong communication skills in English; German language skills are welcome but not required.

What You'll Find at GlassPoint

- Meaningful work that contributes directly to global decarbonization efforts with opportunities to take ownership and make an impact from day one.
- An inclusive, collaborative, and international working environment.
- Colleagues who support one another, share knowledge, and celebrate success together.
- Challenging projects that encourage innovation, growth, and continuous learning.
- The chance to help scale a technology that is transforming how heavy industry generates heat and steam.

We are committed to providing an inclusive working environment where everyone is treated with respect, feels valued, and has the opportunity to contribute their best work.
